english: The sum $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{n^2+1}{n}\left(\frac34\right)^n$ can be written as $\alpha+\log_e\beta$, where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are positive integers. Then the value of $\alpha\beta$ is ______.
hindi: योग $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{n^2+1}{n}\left(\frac34\right)^n$ को $\alpha+\log_e\beta$ के रूप में लिखा जा सकता है, जहाँ $\alpha$ तथा $\beta$ धनात्मक पूर्णांक हैं। तब $\alpha\beta$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Sum $=12+\log_e4$; if $\alpha+\log_e\beta=12+\log_e4$ then $\beta=4e^{12-\alpha}$, an integer only for $\alpha=12$ ($e^k$ is irrational for integer $k\neq0$): $\alpha=12,\ \beta=4$
solution_full: Split the general term: $\dfrac{n^2+1}{n}x^n=nx^n+\dfrac{x^n}{n}$ with $x=\dfrac34$; both resulting series converge since $|x|<1$.
The first is an arithmetico-geometric series: with $S=\displaystyle\sum_{n\ge1}nx^n$, $S-xS=\displaystyle\sum_{n\ge1}x^n=\frac{x}{1-x}$, so $S=\dfrac{x}{(1-x)^2}=\dfrac{3/4}{1/16}=12$.
The second is the logarithmic series: $\log_e(1-x)=-\displaystyle\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{x^n}{n}$ for $|x|<1$, so $\displaystyle\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(3/4)^n}{n}=-\log_e\frac14=\log_e4$.

Uniqueness: if $\alpha+\log_e\beta=12+\log_e4$ with positive integers $\alpha,\beta$, then $\beta=4e^{12-\alpha}$. For an integer $k\neq0$, $e^k$ is irrational, so $\beta$ is an integer only when $\alpha=12$, and then $\beta=4$.
originality_note: New: one series whose term splits into an AGP part and a logarithmic-series part, with the final representation alpha + log_e beta made unique by the irrationality of e^k (way 5: AGP linked with the log series). Closest known: separate exercises on sum n x^n and on sum x^n/n. Different because: both appear in one term through (n^2 + 1)/n, and the answer needs the split and the uniqueness argument.
blueprint_concepts: Sum of an Arithmetico Geometric Progression

concept_use.Sum of an Arithmetico Geometric Progress: The part sum n(3/4)^n is an AGP summed by S - xS to 12.
concept_use.Exponential and logarithmic series (e^x,: The part sum (3/4)^n/n is the series of -log_e(1 - x) at x = 3/4, giving log_e 4.
